title: 10 years of coding, this was the first time I leaned heavily on AI to take an idea to reality.
author: Grox_are_shitty
selftext:
Hey! So after some reluctance, I decided to create a workflow with a mix of astra, sol, meshy, and suno. For a simple roguelike idea. Basically you have a pirate ship and sail the seas hunting other ships, stealing, scavenging, and trying to upgrade your ship through a semi RNG system. I am quite happy with the results so far after about a week of work.

I could use some help testing, and would love to know what others think of it, what I should add, and if the gameplay loop is actually fun.

Its a web based game that I am hosting for free on itch. I call it "Boat! A Pirate Roguelike"

https://nateharmsfpv.itch.io/boat

replies.author: wirthmore
replies.body: The wind angle already has a big effect on speed, but what may be more immersive is a tell-tale like a pennant on the top of a sail that points downwind, so the user doesn't need to keep their eye on the HUD on the top left. Different ship models respond differently to relative wind angles; square-rigged ships are terrible at sailing into the wind, while other models like sloops suffer very little. The deeper the game gets, a user can take advantage of these differences in tactics.

comments.author: StoicKerfuffle
comments.body:
Great game, I'd honestly pay for that. (How much, I dunno, just saying I would.) The operation is intuitive, the play is interesting and fun.

\- The verticality of the shots was unclear to me, I could tell the waves altered it but I wasn't sure how. Maybe I'm just a dummy and I'd get it in time, maybe I missed how the firing lines show me it, I'm just giving you the perspective of "idiot trying the game for 2 minutes," which is an important aspect, you gotta grab people before they leave.

\- A ramming mechanic. A bow ramming a broadside should produce devastating damage, a side-to-side bump should do nothing (as currently the case), and so forth. Factor in ship size/mass too. 

\- Consider historical scenarios. Don't try to make them perfectly historically accurate, just try to fit the vibe of how people think of the battles. If you just send the AI off for examples of battles from The Age of Sail with tactical maps of how they unfolded, you'll have a good basis.

replies.author: Grox_are_shitty
replies.body:
Thank you for taking the time to give it a try.

Right now I have the verticality set to be very forgiving an nearly meaningless, mostly because timing against the waves became infuriating to play with. Im still trying to work out a solution for that.

Ramming is something im working on currently funny enough, that should be a more balanced feature soon.

That is a great idea, I'll take a deeper dive into some real examples.

Thanks for the feedback, it is appreciated!

comments.author: wirthmore
comments.body:
I enjoyed it. I like the gameplay aspect of leading a shot ahead of the enemy's current position. 

1. Recommendation: The gameplay is arcade-like so the functions that require extra coordination and simultaneous button-pressing are not fun and don't match the free-flowing combat and navigation 
   1. The floating items should be picked up automatically if within range and below 4 knots
   2. The docking should happen automatically if below 4 knots if within range and below 4 knots. Also the docking collision detection is too small: one side of the dock is a target, but not the other side, which feels arbitrary and time-consuming when the wrong side is picked. Exiting the dock: if you don't want to teleport the ship out of the dock range, have a boolean or code flag that requires the player to leave the port area or some set distance before the dock is auto-detected again to prevent re-opening the dock UI over and over
2. Difficulty ramp is non-existent, but that's polish. The weather, waves, density of enemies are set to high right at the start (increasing the arcade-like feel, but like mentioned above, conflicts with the functions that require careful coordination
3. The cannons being ready needs to be more obvious.
4. Mixing metric and nautical measurements breaks the immersion. 
5. Judgement call: The cannons all firing in perfect sequence is also immersion-breaking. The visuals and audio can stagger and have slightly different timing offsets, the gameplay code can be as accurate as you want. As it is the cannonballs may be pixel-accurate but it never looks that way, I sink ships when appeared to be hit by only a single shot. In my opinion, a more natural, human-like staggered and slightly random timing of the effect in visuals and audio is more pleasing than computerized representation of all cannons firing in perfect order and timing. As an added benefit it's also less repetitive.

replies.author: Grox_are_shitty

This is fantastic feedback. Thank you for taking the time to write this out. I will work on implementing changes based on your recommendations.

Did you find the difficulty was too low, or too high at the beginning?
